li.label: my field given up
li.description: The council let the field go back to grass. I had it marked out to the last row.

li.label: the field sown at last
li.description: The empty field has seed in it again. It looks like somebody's field now.

li.label: the council heard me about the field
li.description: I asked for the field to grow what the colony is short of, and the council said yes.

li.label: the herd thinned
li.description: The council marked some of the herd for the butcher. I know the hay won't stretch. I raised them all the same.

li.label: hay that won't last
li.description: The council kept every animal, and I've counted the hay. Some of them will go hungry before spring.

li.label: a day off after the road
li.description: Home from the road and the council gave me a day to myself. My feet are grateful.

li.label: told them about the road
li.description: I sat down and told someone what the road was like, all of it. It helped to say it.

li.label: back to work off the road
li.description: Days on the road, and the first thing anyone said when I got back was what needed doing.

li.label: doubts talked through
li.description: Someone sat with me and let me say every doubt I had out loud. I feel steadier for it.

li.label: left alone with my doubts
li.description: The council said my faith is my own business. Maybe it is. It's lonely business.

li.label: named the faith's guide
li.description: The council asked me to guide the faith. I hope I'm worth it.

li.label: passed over as guide
li.description: The council chose someone else to guide the faith. I'd have done it well.

li.label: the trees by the wall cut down
li.description: Those trees were the only shade on that side of the colony. Now there's a field of stumps.

li.label: an open flank
li.description: I told the council what the ground outside the wall looks like to someone with a rifle. It's still there.

li.label: the woodpile day
li.description: We brought the winter's wood in together and stacked it by the wall. My arms ache and the pile is taller than I am.

li.label: the night of lights
li.description: A light by every grave, and the colony standing among them a while. Nobody we lost was left in the dark.

li.label: the mending day
li.description: A day of putting right what the year broke. Everything creaks a little less, and so do I.

li.label: the winter tales
li.description: Our own year told back to us in the dark, the bad parts and the good. I hadn't known it was a story until I heard it.

li.label: a hunting season
li.description: Every morning more of the land's animals marked to die. I can't stand it.

li.label: the hunters out every day
li.description: The hunters go out every morning now. I'd rather they didn't.

li.label: a hunting season
li.description: Meat laid by before the cold. That's sense.

li.label: the hunting season
li.description: Out at first light with the hunters, every day. This is the best time of the year.

li.label: the trees coming down
li.description: A morning's trees marked to be felled, every day, for the woodpile. The woods are going.

li.label: wood for the winter
li.description: Axes from first light. My shoulders know it's autumn.

li.label: wood for the winter
li.description: The woodpile grows every day. We won't be cold this year.

li.label: a full woodpile
li.description: Wood stacked to the eaves before the first snow. I sleep better just looking at it.

li.label: picking in the brush
li.description: Every morning out in the thorns for a few berries. It isn't worth the scratches.

li.label: foraging days
li.description: Out picking in the brush when there's real work waiting.

li.label: foraging days
li.description: Whatever the land gives, we take in while it's ripe. It feels like the old way of things.

li.label: the land's harvest
li.description: Berries and roots and the land's own harvest, a basket every morning. I love these days.

li.label: the lamps out at night
li.description: Every lamp in the colony switched off at eleven. I work at night, and now I work in the dark.

li.label: saving the power
li.description: Dark corridors after eleven. I keep walking into things.

li.label: saving the power
li.description: The batteries last the night now. It's only dark while we're asleep.

li.label: a dark, quiet colony
li.description: Every lamp out at night and nothing humming. I sleep like a stone.

li.label: every faith the same to the council
li.description: The council treats the colony's own ideoligion as one among many. It isn't one among many to me.

li.label: every faith its evening
li.description: Other ideoligions' evenings in our colony. I don't mind, quite.

li.label: every faith its evening
li.description: My ideoligion has its evening here too, and nobody minds. That matters.

li.label: a welcome for my faith
li.description: The council gave my ideoligion its evening, the same as theirs. I feel at home here for the first time.
